questions.question: Explain manufacturing and the meaning of value added, with an example.
questions.expected_answer: Manufacturing is turning raw materials or components into finished products. Value added is the difference between the value of the finished product and the cost of the raw materials, created by labour, skill and equipment, e.g. R80 of fabric made into a R400 dress (R320 value added).

questions.question: A baker makes 50 muffins. Ingredients R150, labour R80, electricity and packaging R20. Calculate cost per muffin, and profit if all are sold at R10.
questions.expected_answer: Total cost = R250. Cost per muffin = R250 ÷ 50 = R5. Sales = 50 × R10 = R500. Profit = R500 − R250 = R250 (R5 per muffin).

questions.question: Give two differences between trading and manufacturing.
questions.expected_answer: Trader buys finished goods and resells them unchanged; manufacturer makes the goods. Trading needs less equipment and skill and is quicker to start; manufacturing needs skills, equipment and time but adds more value and can create a unique product. Trading mark-ups are often small with high competition.
